15.text: Clio Consults Notebook saying This sounds like persistent sync interference, even after comprehensive troubleshooting. Since standard steps like clearing cache and reinstalling didn't resolve missing folders and files, the issue is likely tied to the local installation's file system or the online document manifest.Here are the next steps:Perform Advanced Local Cache Cleanup (Targeting Database Files - macOS): Sometimes the manual clear cache action fails, or a specific database file remains corrupted. You can manually delete the database files on a Mac to force a complete re-indexing of metadata when the app restarts.Quit the Clio Desktop app (Gear icon > Quit).Open Spotlight Search (Command + Space).Enter ~/Library/Application Support.In the Clio Launcher folder, locate and delete the files ending with .db (e.g., drive-*.db).Restart the computer and launch the Clio Desktop App. This forces the drive metadata to resync from scratch.Check File Naming/Path Length: Since you are on macOS, ensure the file path length is not exceeding the 1024-character limit, or the single folder name is over 255 characters. If so, the documents won't display in Clio Drive. Also check for unsupported special characters like # or / in folder/file names.If the Issue Persists, Start a #help-cs-consult: If performing the manual local database cleanup does not resolve the issue, the folders are likely missing from the core document manifest and a Technical Escalations (TE) admin task is required to force a rebuild.Provide the missing Matter ID(s) and Contact ID(s).Request that a member of TE run the Drive Repopulate Manifests Task. (You must ensure no users are actively using Clio Drive or have documents open before running this task).

15.text: This is what Clio Consults Notebook when said I couldn't find any files with You would find files ending with .db in the Clio Drive cache directory, specifically the local database files used by the Clio Desktop app. These database files are typically named following the pattern drive-{userid}.db (or something similar, containing .db extension) and are found in the following location on a Mac or PC:macOS Path: ~/Library/Application Support/Clio Launcher/Windows Path: %AppData%\Roaming\Clio Launcher\These .db files are part of the cached data and store important information for the Drive, such as a list of all folders and documents (the manifest). Deleting these files after quitting the Clio Desktop App can force a complete re-indexing and resolve issues with missing folders or files not displaying correctly in Clio Drive, although deleting files from the AppData folder is generally advised against unless guided by Technical Escalated teams to prevent potential data loss.

37.author: Gosia Jamka
37.text: This is what I got.The system limitation is that you can only designate one firm user as the fee recipient per contingency fee award. Therefore, directly adding a second "award" will duplicate the total recovered amount in the system.To address the split fee without inflating the total recovery:1. Record the single lump-sum award under the primary attorney.2. Manually calculate the second attorney’s portion of the legal fee.3. Record that calculated amount as a separateFlat Rate time entry under the second attorney's name on the matter

37.author: Melissa Baumann
37.text: Okay yes I got something similar! Instead of strictly using the 'Award' functionality, attorneys can record their portion of the earned fee as a separate item:• Create Flat Rate entries: Attorneys can manually calculate the specific dollar amount of the fee they earned and enter that figure as a Flat Rate time entry assigned under their user profile. If you use this approach, you must manually ensure that the total of these individual flat rate entries equals the total contingency fee owed to the firm.• Contingency Time Entry Adjustment: Time entries on contingency matters are marked as non-billable by default, but this setting can be unchecked if the firm needs to bill activities. These entries often default to a $0.00 rate, which can then be manually updated to reflect the fee amount owed to that specific attorney.

37.author: Melissa Baumann
37.text: Just testing in demo to determine if flat rate time entry can be added to the matter directly or has to be a change made in user profile

37.author: Melissa Baumann
37.text: Okay! So I just don't know how to fill out that time entry, since it bills at an hourly rate by default: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YeBMuFDL3zdhyBHF8i3GAtf_CZcf0_9O/view?usp=drive_linkDo you think that makes sense? I'm not sure else to record it as a "flat fee"

37.author: Gosia Jamka
37.text: To avoid the default hourly rate when recording this allocation:1. Create a Flat Rate Activity Category: Navigate to Activities > Manage Categories and select New category.2. Set the Category type to Time entry category.3. Set the Billing method to Fixed rate (or Flat Rate). You can leave the specific rate blank or set it to $0.00.4. Create the Time Entry: Have the second attorney create a New Time Entry on the matter.5. Select this new Flat Rate Activity Category.6. Enter the agreed-upon amount of the fee split (the manually calculated portion) directly into the Rate field (or equivalent amount field for that entry) and set the quantity to 1 (as is standard for flat rate entries).

39.text: Based on Notebook:The Clio Manage (web version) works because it uses a standard browser session, but the Clio Desktop App uses an embedded browser within the app for its specific OAuth login flow. 69.text: To rerun the conflict check without including Clio Grow categories, follow these steps:Initiate the Conflict Check:Go to the Contacts tab in Clio Manage.Click the Conflict Checks subtab.Select Run Conflict Check.Set Search Parameters:On the conflict check page, enter the search details (e.g., Person, Company, or Keyword).Avoid selecting any options or categories related to Clio Grow data.Customize Search Scope:Click More Details to adjust search preferences and ensure only Clio Manage data is included.Generate Results:Once the parameters are set, click Generate Results to complete the conflict check using only Clio Manage data.

95.text: Just checking a bit and this is typically how it detects duplicates and works:- The deduplication logic checks for “true duplicates,” meaning the events must be completely identical across all relevant fields.- The fields compared typically include: title, start time, end time, location, description, and possibly attendees. If any of these fields differ, the entries are not considered duplicates.- The tool does not exclude events based on their origin (e.g., Office 365 sync vs. manual entry). Synced events are treated the same as native Clio events for deduplication purposes.- Only exact matches are flagged. For example, two events with the same name but different times or descriptions will not be deduplicated.- The tool will delete the newer duplicate and retain the older one.- Some events may not be deduplicated if they have associated data (e.g., matters, notes, communications), but this is more relevant for contacts than calendar events. (edited)

155.text: This sounds like a synchronization problem with the operating bank account mapping after a recent external update. Although the account displays as connected on the settings screen, the link status (expired) and missing option under "New Charge" indicate a broken link between Clio and LawPay.Recommended Solution:Advise the customer to try resolving the conflict by performing a focused disconnection and reconnection of only the specific bank account within the Clio settings:1. In Clio Manage, navigate to Settings > Online Payments2. Locate the relevant operating account and click the downward arrow next to Edit3. Select Disconnect from online payments4. If prompted with the warning about stopping payment plans, the customer should proceed only if they are aware they may need to re-create any affected payment plans5. After disconnecting, immediately reconnect the account by following the prompts to map it back to the existing LawPay operating accountWarning: This process relies on reconnecting the bank account and should not involve disconnecting the entire LawPay integration (by disabling Clio Payments). Disconnecting the overall integration is explicitly discouraged for troubleshooting and requires advanced steps to restore (edited)

168.author: Qasim Khan
168.text: The issue of Clio Drive search only showing individual files, rather than folders, is a challenge inherent in how Windows File Explorer searches network drives like Clio Drive.Resolution/Workaround:Clio Drive search utilizes the search functionality of Finder (Mac) and File Explorer (Windows) to search document headings within synced folders, including closed mattersExpected Behavior: While searching finds files, there is no current feature to allow searching for the location/folder path of a document when using global searchThis is a known limitation and a Feature Request (FR) (edited)

181.author: Lola Tonade
181.text: found this on notebookTo determine when a user was deactivated in Clio Manage, there are a few primary methods:1. Check the Firm Feed (Internal Check): The Firm Feed should reflect when a user was deactivated. However, if the deactivation occurred long ago (e.g., in 2022), the customer may not want to scroll through the entire feed.2.Check the Admin Panel (AP) (Internal Check): The Account Admin Panel (AP) keeps records of users, and disabled/deactivated users still appear there. TheDate Updated on the user's AP page sometimes indicates the time of a major change, such as deactivation. You can access a user's details via the Admin Panel URL using their user ID.3. Check Login Activity (User-Facing Check): The firm administrator can check login activity by going to Settings > Security & Compliance > Log In Activity. This page shows the user's last access date and activity details, which can serve as a close workaround for the deactivation date.4.Backend Logs (Technical Escalation): If user-facing tools or Admin Panel checks do not provide the exact deactivation date, Technical Escalations (TE) can search backend logs. However, note that these logs typically only go back about 60 to 90 days.There isno dedicated user-facing feature that explicitly provides the exact deactivation date on the "Manage Users" page.For additional assistance, or if looking for information beyond basic Admin Panel checks, you may need to consult:#help-cs-consults or #help-security.

237.text: 1. Quit the Clio Desktop App: Use the Gear Icon > Quit option if possible. If it is unresponsive, use Task Manager to force close the application.2.Uninstall the Program:    ◦ Go to Control Panel (or Settings > Apps & features).    ◦ Under Programs, selectUninstall a program.    ◦ Find and uninstall the Clio Desktop App/Launcher.3. Manually Delete Remaining Files (Crucial Step):    ◦ Search for %AppData% in the Windows Start Menu or File Explorer address bar.    ◦ Navigate to theAppData folder.    ◦ Go to the Local folder and ensure the clio_launcher or Clio Launcher folders have been deleted.    ◦ Return to theAppData folder and go to the Roaming folder.    ◦ Ensure theClio Launcher folder is deleted here as well.4.Note: This process should only be done when standard troubleshooting fails, as deleting these folders can delete locally saved documents and logs if they were not successfully uploaded to Clio Manage.5.Restart the Computer.6.Reinstall: Download a fresh installer from the Documents tab in Clio Manage and reinstall the Clio Desktop App.If the missing folders issue persists after a clean reinstall and allowing adequate time for the initial sync:• Check Performance Settings: Ensure the settings within the Clio Desktop App aren't limiting display. In the app, go to Settings (Gear icon) > Preferences > Improve performance, and check the "Maximum number of files displayed in a folder" setting (we generally recommend 5000 or less).•Escalate to TE: If the folders are visible in Clio Manage but still missing in Clio Drive across multiple users/devices after a clean install, this suggests a deeper sync or manifest issue. Start a #help-cs-consult to check if the manifest needs to be rebuilt by Technical Escalations

263.text: Additional context for this swarm (if provided) can be found below:SS : https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aXxSmDXtbHYonZDPZn5ZW-ACwyFX9SIH?usp=sharingNotebook response: This 1-cent discrepancy is typically caused by a rounding difference in how Clio calculates line items versus the total invoice.Why this happens:• Calculation Logic: Clio calculates taxes and discounts on each individual line item using precise values (often more than 2 decimal places).• Display Rounding: For the invoice display, these individual amounts are rounded to 2 decimal places.• The Discrepancy: When the system sums the "Invoice Total," it may be aggregating the raw, precise values, whereas the "Matter Total" or the visible line items might be summing the rounded display values (or vice versa). This often results in a $0.01 difference.Workarounds:• Manual Adjustment: Edit a line item price or the tax amount on the bill by $0.01 to force the totals to align.• Apply a Discount: Add a $0.01 discount to the invoice to balance the total.If these workarounds do not resolve the issue, please start a #help-cs-consult

269.text: Ok, this is what I found:This sounds like an issue where a specific section on the Contact Edit page has incomplete data, preventing the save action without displaying a clear error message.Suggested Troubleshooting Steps:1. Check Billing Preferences:    ◦ Ask the customer to click Edit on the contact.    ◦ Scroll down to the Billing preferences section.    ◦ Check if a custom rate has been added but is missing a Firm User or Rate. 308.text: Also, Notebook response :Troubleshooting Steps1. Check for Pending Invitations:    ◦ Go to Settings > Manage Users in Clio Manage.    ◦ Look under the Pending tab.    ◦ If you see an invite for that email, Revoke/Delete the invitation.    ◦ Resend the invitation. This often clears the "stuck" state and allows the user to set up their account properly.2. Check for Deactivated Users:    ◦ In Settings > Manage Users, filter by Deactivated or All Users.    ◦ If the email belongs to a deactivated user, you cannot create a new user with the same email. 337.text: Historical vs. Live Data: The standard Originating Attorney Revenue Report is a historical report. It provides a snapshot of data based on the date range selected (e.g., payments made within that period for bills issued in that period) [cite: 15, 369]. Custom reports often pull data differently or may not adhere to the exact same "historical" logic regarding invoice and payment dates.

Contact the Bank: The client should contact the bank associated with the card they are trying to use to ensure there are no blocks on the transaction.3. Contact Affirm Support: If the issue persists, the client must contact Affirm Customer Support directly, as they manage the loan approval and disputes.4. 353.author: Sohaib Naseem
353.text: Review and Classify Each MatchYou need to click into that specific unreviewed search result to see the matches. For every name or term the system flagged, a user must make a decision:If it is NOT a conflict: Mark the match as "Not a Conflict" or "Cleared".If it IS a conflict: Mark the match as "Conflict".overall check may still remain in an unreviewed state until a final decision is made on all potential matches.(edited)

353.author: Sohaib Naseem
353.text: Once every single matched item in that search run has been marked with a final decision (Conflict or Not a Conflict), the overall conflict check status will update, and the error will disappear. You should then be able to proceed with opening the new matter or client file.

362.text: This is what I found on Notebook:This is expected behavior. The Outlook Add-in does not automatically move matter folders in Outlook when the matter status is changed in Clio Manage. Clio Manage cannot update the user's mailbox folders directly; the action must be performed from the Outlook Add-in side.Solutions:1. Manual Move: The user can manually drag and drop the matter folder from the "Open" folder to the "Closed" folder in Outlook.2. Trigger Update: File a new email to that specific matter using the Outlook Add-in. The Add-in will detect the status change during the filing process and move the folder to the "Closed" section.

381.text: Additional context for this swarm (if provided) can be found below:** What's the end goal?To clarify if this is intended behaviour of Australian Clio Payment Deposits** When/where is it happening? (List steps)When firms receive their Bank deposit from Stripe, via online payments that were made by clients some days ago, this deposit is a lump sum that includes payments for multiple mattersIn Australia, there are transaction fees/card fees that occur as part of online payments and by default a firm will absorb these fees themselves. I have taken screenshots of the two Clio Invoices that this firms first Online Payment Deposit relates to as well as a screenshot of their Bank Statement next to Clios Online Deposit Report. LINKhttps://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1jVy8A4L8lYqyjCAOeATE3xCY518CPdA7?usp=sharing** What do you need/where are you stuck?The deposit report shows there was a total of $3.13 deducted from the total $1750.43 as Fees, however it appears as though it was deducted directly from the Deposit amount, rather than reflecting as a separate Debit line  from the bank account to identify the fees separate to the client payments. Is this the intended behaviour of when fees are deducted via online payments? If so, are there any recommendations on how a firm should include these details when reconciling their Office account? - I assume they would need to add manual debits of each Fee when reconciling to balance their books. (In most cases, this is done in Xero in Australia)This query was initially raised as the accountant of the Firm could not accurately identify the correct bank transactions against the Clio Invoices without comparing each deposit from the Clio Deposit Report

381.author: Sarah Aoukaty
381.text: That’s intended, Clio Payments are always deposited net of fees if on a daily fee schedule. The deposit report is what they use for reconciliation purposes to identify which payments and debits are included in the payout to their bank account on each respective day. They can switch to a monthly fee schedule if they’d like the fees removed separately in bulk.

Comparing reports between Clio and integrated accounting systems is generally not recommended, but I wanted to confirm if this is correct as client says that they should match and that this issue started in July.

453.author: Service Cloud
453.text: A swarm member record was created in Salesforce for each swarm member:  @habibat.buhari.

453.author: Habibat Buhari
453.text: The discrepancy is expected. These reports are built on different logic and criteria. the Revenue Report reflects Clio’s billing and collected amounts, while QuickBooks’ Income by Customer reflects accounting income as posted in QuickBooks. Because of these different purposes and calculation methods, the totals will not match, and comparing them directly isn’t recommended.

453.author: Carlotta Crestanello
453.text: Informed him about that but he says that it's impossible that the difference is $90k

453.author: Carlotta Crestanello
453.text: Difference between June and October, he wants to show us that the difference is becoming bigger and bigger each month

453.author: Habibat Buhari
453.text: These reports are not supposed to be compared. Even in Clio, Every report is unique in the criteria it uses to calculate financial data. This means that comparing different types of reports is not recommended.

453.author: Habibat Buhari
453.text: The Revenue Report is invoice-based, while QBO Income is payment- and posting-based.

453.author: Carlotta Crestanello
453.text: I informed him about this but unfortunately he insists that the difference is becoming bigger every month and that is not supposed to happen and it was not happening before July 2025

510.text: Steps for the Customer1. Disable 2FA: If 2FA is currently enabled, they must disable it first to restart the setup process.2. Start Setup: Go to Settings > Security and select Set up for the Authenticator App.3. Scan Simultaneously: When the QR code appears on the computer screen, scan that same QR code with the Microsoft Authenticator app on Device 1 AND Device 2.4. Finalize: Both devices will now generate identical codes. Enter the code to verify and save.Important Notes• Cannot Add Later: Once the setup is complete, the QR code cannot be viewed again. To add a device later, they must disable and re-enable 2FA to generate a new QR code.

(List steps): The issue they are having is linking the expense they have added on a matter (ex GST) to an office transaction, indicating it has now been paid out of their Office account, like a 3rd party invoiceIssue is, the payment is made with Tax/GST included and Clio doesnt allow users to record this payment + link the transaction as the expense amount is less than the transaction amount (pre-GST)This may be a product gap that has been in Clio for a long time now.The workaround is to add the expense against the matter with GST included (with the setting to Do Not Apply Tax)However this is not a efficient workaround, as with QBO or Xero sync'd, the accounting data for these transactions do not reflect back - What do you need/where are you stuck?:It was advised to check with TE to confirm whether this is a known product gap and to determine next steps or potential solutions.

The customer said he got Clio specifically for the client portal.- However, he realized that his clients can't set a password or enable 2FA for client portal- I advised cx that the portal uses a "passwordless" system. Clients log in by entering their email address and receiving a one-time secure link (Magic Link) via email. 552.text: So the parameters on this one can be a little tricky:UnbilledThe Unbilled column will display a summary of Unbilled Time and Unbilled Expenses by dollar when reported on by Money. Billed refers to entries placed on Bills in Unpaid or Paid status. When reported on by Time, a summary of hours is displayed. When restricted by Date, the Billed column will display amounts represented on invoices whose Issue Date is within the selected Date Range.

554.text: Since the standard troubleshooting steps (creating and deleting a journal entry) did not resolve the issue, the internal sequence number in QuickBooks Online (QBO) likely still conflicts with an existing record.Workaround:1. Save and then Delete this new journal entry.5. Go back to Clio Manage > Settings > Bill Syncing and click Retry on the error. (edited)

636.author: Qasim Khan
636.text: Debit Column (The Payment): This column lists the actual payment amount received and applied to the bill. It represents the lump sum of money coming in (e.g., a check or credit card payment)Credit Column (The Allocation): This column breaks down how that payment was used. It lists the specific line items (Services, Expenses, Taxes) on the invoice that were paid off by the Debit amountTimekeeper Allocation: Timekeepers are associated with the work performed (Services). Therefore, you will only see timekeeper names on the Credit side next to the specific service line items they generated. The Debit side is just the total payment source and is not inherently linked to a specific user until it is distributed to these line items

636.author: Qasim Khan
636.text: Debits on the Credit Side: Debits and Credits will not appear on the same side because they represent opposite sides of the transaction (Payment Received vs. Debt Settled). The report lists the Payment (Debit) first, followed by the breakdown of what it paid for (Credits)

636.author: Qasim Khan
636.text: The Transaction column will list the source of the payment (e.g., "Direct Payment", "Credit Card", "Trust Account") and the Date column shows when it was applied

642.text: This is what Notebook said:Based on the error code 6140, this is a Duplicate Document Number Error. This means the reference number associated with the trust transaction in Clio (Pa nd12-15-26df Trans) already exists on a Journal Entry in QuickBooks Online (QBO).Solution:To resolve Error 6140 for Trust Transactions, please guide the customer through the following steps in QBO and Clio:1. (This resets the internal sequencing).2. In Clio Manage:    ◦ Go to Settings > Bill Syncing.    ◦ Scroll down to the Sync Status / Sync Failures section.    ◦ Click Retry next to the error.

655.author: Gosia Jamka
655.text: This is what I found in Notebook:Troubleshooting Steps:1. Verify Account Match: Ensure the Dropbox account used to upload the documents matches the specific Dropbox account connected in Clio Manage (Settings > Documents > Document Sources).2. Test with a Matter: Ask the customer to try the same workflow with a Matter folder (create a matter, click the Dropbox tab to create the folder, upload a file to that folder in Dropbox). 683.text: Hey Abigail, that is not the expected behavior.

683.author: Qasim Khan
683.text: Disconnecting and reconnecting a document integration like Dropbox, especially after renaming the original folder, Clio creates a brand new "Clio" folder to establish the sync. The system does not automatically transfer files from the old (renamed) folder to the new on

683.text: They said some files were transferred from the old folder. I tried to tell them to manually transfer the files but they want to know why some files were automatically moved while others weren't.

683.author: Qasim Khan
683.text: 1. Ask the customer to locate the new "Clio" folder in their Dropbox.2. They must manually move the contents (client/matter folders) from the "Clio DNU" folder into the new "Clio" folder3. Once moved, the files should begin to populate in Clio Manage.

683.author: Qasim Khan
683.text: Are you on SS with customer

683.author: Qasim Khan
683.text: Can he send us an SS of the files that were transferred automatically to the new folder.

683.text: yeah, I am. Okay

683.author: Qasim Khan
683.text: Thank you!

683.author: Billy Yu
683.text: I don't want to make any assumptions with anyones understanding of this sync but just wanted to be clear that the Dropbox integration is a view from Clio Manage into the files thats stored in Dropbox within the Clio folder. The files in Dropbox are not actually synced and saved into Clio Manage. (edited)

683.author: Qasim Khan
683.text: you're correct!

683.author: Qasim Khan
683.text: They're simply just appearing/view through the connected path folder between Clio and Dropbox.

683.author: Billy Yu
683.text: Just a common misunderstanding i've seen agents have.

683.author: Qasim Khan
683.text: So if customer said some files transferred over as result of disconnecting and reconnecting, that would be incorrect.

683.author: Qasim Khan
683.text: The new Clio folder that had been created in dropbox should be empty otherwise.

712.text: For a Mac user unable to locate Clio Drive (often referred to as "localhost" or under "Locations" in Finder), please try the following steps. Note that on Mac, it does not typically mount as the "A: drive" like on Windows, but rather as a mounted network location.

712.author: Gosia Jamka
712.text: Troubleshooting Steps:1. Check Finder Preferences:    ◦ Open Finder.    ◦ Click Finder in the top menu bar > Settings (or Preferences).    ◦ Go to the Sidebar tab.    ◦ Under Locations, ensure Connected servers is checked. This is often disabled by default and hides the drive2. Verify SSL Certificate:    ◦ Open the Clio Desktop App.    ◦ Toggle Drive OFF and then back ON.    ◦ Watch for a system prompt asking to trust a certificate. If it appears, select Always Trust3. Manual Mount (Workaround):    ◦ Open the Clio Desktop App > Settings (gear icon). Note the Port number listed (e.g., 58584).    ◦ In Finder, click Go > Connect to Server (or Cmd+K).    ◦ Type http://localhost:[PORT]/Clio Drive (replace [PORT] with the number from settings).    ◦ Click Connect. Select "Guest" if prompted (edited)

746.text: I'll share just in case:To whitelist Clio in Outlook and Gmail, follow these steps:For Outlook: Open Outlook and go to Settings.Navigate to Junk Email or Spam Settings.Add Clio's email addresses (e.g., notifications@clio.com) to the Safe Senders List.Save your changes.For Gmail: Open Gmail and click the gear icon to access Settings. 765.author: Sonia Czerniawski
765.text: If you see a "Save As" option or prompt when using Clio Launcher, it typically relates to one of two scenarios: standard functionality for creating local copies or a specific setting issue within Adobe Acrobat.1. Standard "Save As" FunctionalityWhen you are editing a document opened via Clio Launcher (e.g., in Word), using Save As performs a specific function different from the standard Save.Save: Saves your changes directly to the document in Clio Manage.Save As: Saves the changes to Clio Manage and saves a copy of the file in the Clio Launcher root folder on your computer.Important: If you use "Save As" and select a folder other than the Clio Launcher root folder, the changes may not be updated in Clio Manage.2. Adobe Acrobat Forcing "Save As"If you are editing a PDF and Adobe forces you to use "Save As" instead of letting you simply "Save," this is likely caused by a security setting in Adobe called Protected Mode.Cause: Adobe is launching with "Protected Mode Enabled at Startup," which prevents direct saving back to the temporary location Clio Launcher uses.Resolution:In Adobe, go to Edit (or the Menu icon).Select Preferences.Click on Security (Enhanced) in the left sidebar.Uncheck the box for Enable Protected Mode at Startup.Click OK and restart Adobe.If that does not resolve the issue, you can also try disabling "Automatically save document changes" under the Documents section of Adobe Preferences.

800.text: Updating the Tax ID (EIN) for Clio Payments is primarily for payment verification and 1099K tax reporting. This change must be handled by emailing payments@clio.com. This specific update does not automatically change the Tax ID printed on invoices unless you also manually update the Tax ID field in your Account and Payment Info settings. 817.author: Billy Yu
817.text: As per Notebook : To generate a report showing client balances as of a specific date in the past, you cannot use the standard Accounts Receivable Report, as it is non-historical (it only shows balances as of today).Instead, you must use the Statements of Account feature.Solution: Generate Statements of Account This feature provides opening balances, closing balances, and the balance owed as of the specific date range you select.1. Navigate to the Billing tab.2. Click the arrow next to the New bills button in the top right.3. Select New statements of account.4. In the Select Date Range field, enter the specific period you wish to report on.    ◦ Note: Any activity before the start date will appear as "Opening Balance." The report will calculate the balance owed as of the end date selected.

(List steps)- What have you tried?     - Troubleshooting steps taken     - Reproduced in demo?     - Link to resources used     - Relevant screenshots/media (e.g. dev tools)- What do you need/where are you stuck?She says she disputed a charge from her lawyer and the Firm lost the dispute.She received an email from her lawyer about it on Dec 5th.When she called her bank to check the money, they are saying they do not see any trace or do not have any update of the result and they are asking for the details to look into it.How long does it take for the funds to be returned back to the client that were initially kept on hold for a dispute?I checked Notebook and got this answer:Here is the breakdown of the fund movement:• Immediate Withdrawal: When a dispute is initiated, Clio is required by card network rules to withdraw the disputed funds from the law firm's operating account immediately and return them to the client's bank.• Client Access: The client's bank typically provides these funds to the client as a provisional credit while the investigation is ongoing.• Final Decision: When the client wins the dispute, that provisional credit simply becomes permanent. There is usually no additional transfer of funds at the time of the "win" decision, as the money was already moved at the start of the process.If the client does not see the funds, they must contact their bank directly, as the bank controls the release of the funds to the cardholder.

864.author: Gosia Jamka
864.text: Here are the troubleshooting steps to resolve why the hard costs are not importing:1. Check Transaction Type: Verify the transaction in QBO is an Expense or Check. If it was recorded as a Bill in QBO, it will not sync to Clio.2. Check Global Activities: If the client has multiple matters, the expense will sync to the main Activities tab (left sidebar) and will not be assigned to a specific matter yet. You must filter by the client name in the main list to find and link it.3. Verify Sync Date: Confirm the expense date (Dec 19) is on or after the "Start import from" date saved in Clio's QBO sync settings.

885.text: Additional context for this swarm (if provided) can be found below:- What's the end goal? Clio investigate these formatting inconsistencies at the database or export level for files from Clio to an Amazon S3 (AWS) bucket.- When/where is it happening? (List steps) The customer is reporting a significant formatting error within their automated Data Escrow backups from Clio to an Amazon S3 (AWS) bucket. Specifically, they have identified an inconsistency in the DATE column for bank transactions and billing backups.The issue is characterized by the following:Inconsistent Date Formats: The system randomly toggles between MM/dd/YY and YYYY-MM-dd formats.Data Corruption: When switching to the YYYY-MM-dd format, the system incorrectly maps the original data order. This results in an invalid MMMM-dd-YY output (for example, generating "2007" or "2008" dates for an account that only has data back to 2019).Potential Standards Conflict: The customer believes this stems from Clio's failure to consistently use the ISO 8601 standard ($YYYY-MM-DD$) across all fields, causing external platforms like AWS or Excel to misinterpret the data.The customer has expressed frustration that they are having to troubleshoot this technical discrepancy manually and is requesting that Clio investigate these formatting inconsistencies at the database or export level.- What have you tried?     - Troubleshooting steps taken: asked customer to confirm that the data is leaving Clio correctly, I recommend checking a manual export directly from our interface. If you click into Exports, you will be provided with the .csv and .ics files generated directly by our system. If the dates in these manual CSV exports appear correctly, it confirms that the formatting issue is occurring during the transfer to or the processing within your Amazon S3 bucket rather than within the Clio database itself.- The customer is reporting that their issue persists despite having both Clio and their local computer settings already set to YYYY-MM-DD. They have identified a potential conflict between Clio's internal formatting and international standards.     - Reproduced in demo?     - Link to resources used     - Relevant screenshots/media (e.g. dev tools) https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dnt2SkI-q4Uv5NFc6yaLKLjm9GzFg2cR/view?usp=drive_link- What do you need/where are you stuck? We need TE to do a deeper dive to confirm the date format Clio uses when sending data to AWS.Insight from consult notebook Based on the sources, the date format Clio uses depends on the specific function or service interacting with AWS (Amazon Web Services):• Data Migrations (Importing to Clio): When populating migration templates (CSVs) to send data to Clio (hosted on AWS), dates must be in MM/DD/YYYY format (e.g., 01/31/2024),,.• API & Backend Logs: When interacting via API or viewing backend logs (e.g., ELK/Kibana on AWS), Clio typically uses the ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-02-11T23:59:59.999Z).• Data Escrow (Amazon S3): When Clio sends data to an Amazon S3 bucket for Data Escrow, client folders are automatically named using the format id.{number} (e.g., id.1054184816) rather than a date format. The backup itself updates weekly,.• Clio Drive (Syncing to AWS): When files are moved or copied into Clio Drive (which syncs to AWS), the "Modified On" date is updated to the current date and time of the upload, rather than preserving the original timestamp.If you are validating billing data via reports, note that report date filters and values generally follow the MM/DD/YYYY format, even for some international region

898.author: Sohaib Naseem
898.text: So remember draft payments can't record payment against them cause they're in draft

898.author: Sohaib Naseem
898.text: must be approved

898.author: Sohaib Naseem
898.text: Disbursing payments also doesn't unlink them from the trust request

898.author: Sohaib Naseem
898.text: If you have disbursed the funds then they can write off the trust and just keep note of the trust request being recorded in error

898.author: Sohaib Naseem
898.text: Payments cannot be edited once they are allocated to a trust request. Ensure your selection is correct before saving changes.

898.author: Melissa Baumann
898.text: Oh yes sorry! We haven't gotten to recording the transaction manually yet, but I'll make sure she approves that draft first.I should've clarified - I figured it wouldn't be possible to remove that $500 payment from the invoice, but was just unsure as to how to handle linking the correct payment to the invoice, because wouldn't this show a total of $3,500 being paid towards a $3,000 balance? And thus client would have a $500 over-payment associated with their account?

898.author: Melissa Baumann
898.text: Sorry I'm saying 'invoice' and 'trust request' but mean the same thing

898.author: Sohaib Naseem
898.text: They would write it off and create a new trust request to account for the correct amount

898.author: Sohaib Naseem
898.text: Due to trust compliance we can't change the trust request or edit it

898.author: Sohaib Naseem
898.text: But disbursing funds ensures we removed the money from the account

898.author: Sohaib Naseem
898.text: So no overpayment

898.author: Melissa Baumann
898.text: Oh! Okay so manually write-off the $2,500 balance owing on that $3,000.00 trust request then?

898.author: Sohaib Naseem
898.text: Yeah they can then recreate the trust request asking for 3000

898.author: Sohaib Naseem
898.text: A new request would replace the one recorded incorrectly

898.author: Sohaib Naseem
898.text: Usually they will get a warning when linking trust amounts to a trust request"Payments cannot be edited once they are allocated to a trust request. Ensure your selection is correct before saving changes."

898.author: Sohaib Naseem
898.text: Just ask them to be careful when doing this step to review details first to prevent user error like this.

898.author: Melissa Baumann

898.text: Right! It shouldn't when writing off a trust request

898.author: Sohaib Naseem
898.text: It simply clears the "Outstanding" request from your Clio ledger.

905.text: Clear Outlook Cache (RoamCache) Corrupted cache files can cause persistence issues.Close Outlook completely.Press the Windows Key + R on the keyboard.Type %localappdata%\Microsoft\Outlook and press Enter.Open the RoamCache folder.Select all files (Ctrl + A) and delete them (this will not delete emails, only temporary cache) Restart Outlook and log in to the Add-in again.

939.text: Here are the available options to resolve this:1. The Affidavit Process (Recommended)To regain access to the account (so they can log in and cancel it themselves, or authorize us to do so), they must submit a notarized affidavit to update the login email address to one they currently have access to.Steps for the Customer:• Create a sworn Affidavit stating the following:• Have the Affidavit notarized.• Send the Affidavit to support@clio.com.Once received, the Support team (specifically the Support Leads or Security team) can verify the document, update the email address on the backend, and allow the customer to reset their password and log in. Stop Payment via Bank (Last Resort)If the customer is unable or unwilling to provide an affidavit and simply wants billing to stop:• They can contact their bank or credit card provider to stop the charges.• After 3 failed payment attempts (and a grace period), the account will automatically move to a Suspended state and eventually be Cancelled for non-payment.Note: We cannot manually cancel the account without the verification provided by the Support Code or the Affidavit.

940.author: Gosia Jamka
940.text: Ok, based on the behaviour described, the customer is likely encountering a mapping issue or a misunderstanding of how Trust transactions sync compared to Operating payments.Solution:1. Clarify the Sync Type: Confirm with the customer that Trust transactions sync to QuickBooks Online (QBO) as Journal Entries, not as "Payments" or "Deposits". The "notebook" advice regarding "Bank Deposits" applies to Invoice Payments (Operating funds) which sync to "Undeposited Funds" and must be moved manually in QBO. This workflowdoes not apply to Trust transactions.2. Verify Account Mapping: Go to Settings > Bill Syncing > Configure in Clio Manage. Ensure the QBO Trust Bank Account is mapped to the exact bank account they are trying to reconcile in QBO, not a sub-account or a separate "Cheque Ledger".3. Check the Transaction in QBO:    ◦ Locate the specific Journal Entry in the QBO register.    ◦ Verify the Date: Is it within the Start/End date of the reconciliation period?    ◦ Verify the Account: Does the Journal Entry actually debit/credit the specific Bank Account being reconciled? If it synced to a different ledger (like a liability account only), it will not appear in the Bank Account reconciliation screen.4.Check Status: In the QBO register, check if the transaction already has a "C" (Cleared) or "R" (Reconciled) status. If it was previously marked, it may not show up as "selectable" depending on QBO filter settings.If the transaction is in the correct ledger, within the correct dates, and unchecked, but still not appearing in the reconciliation window, this may be a QBO display filter issue or a browser cache issue.

1014.author: Dan Kotak
1014.text: The Lead Capture Token acts as an authorization key (like a password) that allows a website or third-party tool to send data to the Clio Grow Lead Inbox. It does not "collect" information itself; rather, the website form must bundle the data into a specific format (JSON) and send it to Clio.If specific fields are not coming over, it is likely because they do not match the strict list of supported fields or because you are trying to map Custom Fields, which are not supported by the Lead Inbox endpoint.How it Works & Supported FieldsThe website sends a "POST" request to Clio. This request must contain the inbox_lead_token and a data object called inbox_lead containing only these specific fields:• from_first (First Name)• from_last (Last Name)• from_email (Email Address)• from_phone (Phone Number)• from_message (Message/Notes)• from_source (Lead Source, e.g., "Website")• referring_url (URL where the form was submitted)Why Fields Might Be Missing1. Unsupported Custom Fields: The Lead Inbox API cannot populate Custom Fields (e.g., "Date of Birth," "Case Type," "Address"). If your website form collects these, the data will be dropped unless it is mapped to a supported field.2. Incorrect Field Names: The code on the website must use the exact names listed above (e.g., sending phone_number instead of from_phone will fail).WorkaroundTo capture data from unsupported fields (like an address or case description), the web developer/tool must combine that text and map it into the from_message field. This ensures the information arrives in the "Notes" section of the lead, even if it doesn't populate a specific field.

I will post here what the task will and will not do.The following restrictions applyThe new interest rate has to be a value between 0.00 and 100.00 (no negative interest)If you have different interest rates for different bills, run the task for one interest rate at a time.All bills in the group below must belong to the same account otherwise they will be excluded from being processed.What the task will do:Sets a new interest on the bill (valid states: draft, awaiting approval, awaiting payment).Sets a new interest period on the bill.Sets a new interest type on the bill.Removes all interest line items on the bill.What the task will not do:Set new interest on bills with partial payments, or that are fully paid.Remove interest from bills that have partial payments, or that are fully paid.Deal with Trust Requests as Trust Requests don't accrue interest.Backfill the interest. 1111.author: Ro Paydar
1111.text: See this summary from Joanna. It's in-depth but it will provide the details regarding what is happening here: New email addresses are commonly added to the suppression list due to hard bounces or complaints when sending via AWS SES. A hard bounce typically occurs when the recipient address does not exist or is invalid. SES automatically adds such addresses to its global suppression list to prevent repeated delivery attempts, which could harm sender reputation and deliverability rates. This suppression can last up to 14 days by default, but can be manually removed if the underlying issue is resolved (e.g. the mailbox is created after the first attempt)For newly created email addresses, it's common for them to bounce if the mailbox isn't fully provisioned or DNS records haven't propagated, leading to immediate suppression upon the first failed delivery attempt. If repeated attempts are made before the mailbox is ready, the address will keep getting re-added to the suppression listAdditionally, if a domain or mailbox has strict anti-spam or throttling rules, or if too many emails are sent in a short window, the provider may reject the messages, causing SES to interpret these as hard bounces and suppress the address.

1130.author: Qasim Khan
1130.text: The error "Duplicate row for custom" typically indicates that the Custom Field being imported is already attached to the Matter or Contact in Clio Manage. This most commonly happens if the Custom Field was created with the "Default" or "Required" checkbox enabled When a field is set to "Default," Clio automatically adds it to every new (and often existing) Matter/Contact. When the CSV import tries to add that same field again to populate the data, the system flags it as a duplicate attempt.

1138.author: Gosia Jamka
1138.text: For Split Billing, funds held at the Matter Level can only be used to pay the Primary Client's portion of the bill. For any other Split Payee (Related Contact), the funds must reside at their specific Client Level to be available for payment.Since you moved the funds to the Matter, they are now inaccessible for the Split Payee's invoice. Additionally, because there are duplicate contacts, the funds might be sitting on the wrong contact record entirely.1. Identify the Correct Contact: Open the split invoice and click on the Split Payee's name to open their contact page. Note the Contact ID in the URL to ensure you are working with the correct record.2. Move Funds Back to Client Level:    ◦ Go to the Matter > Transactions tab where you deposited the funds.    ◦ Disburse (or delete the transaction if not reconciled) to remove the funds from the Matter Level.    ◦ Navigate to the correct Split Payee's Contact > Transactions tab.    ◦ Record a New Transaction (Deposit) into their Trust account.3. Record Payment: Return to the split bill, click Record Payment, and the funds should now be available to apply from the Client Level.

1138.author: Gosia Jamka
1138.text: You cannot change the client (payer) on a split bill once it has been generated. Because the bill is locked to "Katherine 1," you must recreate the bill for "Katherine 2" to access the funds held in her name.1. Void the Incorrect Bill:    ◦ Go to the split bill associated with Katherine 1 (the wrong contact).    ◦ Void the bill. This is necessary to unlock the billing settings for this matter.2. Update Matter Billing Preferences:    ◦ Navigate to the Matter > Edit Matter.    ◦ Scroll down to Billing Preferences.    ◦ In the Split Invoice section, remove Katherine 1.    ◦ Add Katherine 2 (ensure you select the contact ID that holds the funds) and assign the correct percentage/portion.    ◦ Save the matter.3. Generate a New Bill:    ◦ Go to Billing > New Bills.    ◦ Generate the bill for this matter again. This will create a new invoice specifically for Katherine 2.4. Apply the Funds:    ◦ Open the new invoice for Katherine 2.    ◦ Click Record Payment. The funds sitting at her Client Level will now be available to applyLet me know if that works!

1161.author: Qasim Khan
1161.text: Problem 1: Editing a calendar event in Clio (e.g., linking it to a matter or changing the appointment type) triggers Outlook to automatically re-send invites to clients.Cause: When an event is edited in Clio Manage (e.g., adding a Matter), the sync pushes this update to Outlook. Outlook perceives this as a modification to the meeting details. By default, Outlook/Exchange sends updates to all attendees when a meeting is modified to ensure everyone has the current version.Resolution/Workaround: There is no setting within Clio to suppress Outlook's native notification behavior for synced events. The "Don't send email" option in Clio only suppresses Clio's internal notifications, not the external Outlook triggers

1283.author: Keturah B.W.
1283.text: Consults Notebook stated: This is expected behavior and does not need to be fixed. When syncing with QuickBooks Online (QBO), Clio handles Trust transactions differently than Operating/Revenue transactions to maintain strict trust compliance.Why this happens:• Trust Requests do not sync: Unlike revenue bills, Trust Requests generated in Clio do not sync to QBO as invoices.•Journal Entries: Because there is no "Invoice" in QBO to receive a payment against, Clio syncs Trust deposits (and disbursements) as Journal Entries. This entry debits the Trust Bank Account and credits the Trust Liability Account to ensure the ledger remains balanced without treating the funds as revenue.How to handle in QBO: The customer should proceed bymatching the deposit showing in their QBO Bank Feed to the Journal Entry created by Clio. They should not look for a "Received Payment" or "Sales Receipt" for trust transactions.

1295.text: This is what I got from the consults Notebook- Actually, if the payment was processed via the LawPay integration, you typically cannot find an "Edit" button to unlink it yourself. The ability to unlink payments directly is generally limited to Clio Payments.To unlink a payment processed through the LawPay integration, you must request assistance from Technical Escalations.Steps to Resolve:1. Confirm Details: Locate the payment in the Online Payments tab and note the Date, Amount, and Authorization Code.2. Get Written Permission: You must obtain written permission from the Primary Subscriber or an Administrator to unlink the payment.    ◦ Warning: Inform the customer that unlinking this payment via the admin task will delete the payment record from Clio Manage entirely (though it remains in LawPay). They will need to manually record a direct payment in Clio afterwards to keep their books balanced.3. Start a Consult: Post in #help-cs-consult with the account ID, payment details, and confirmation that you have written permission.If you can see an Edit button: It is possible the payment was recorded manually (e.g., "Direct Payment" labeled as LawPay) rather than processed through the integration. In that case, you can simply Delete the payment from the bill's Payments tab.Trust, but Verify: Seismic: Playbook: The LawPay Integration Slack: Clio Support Help Channel

1307.author: Qasim Khan
1307.text: This is a known behavior with newer versions of QuickBooks Desktop (2019 and later). QBD now enforces a rule where the date on individual line items must match the invoice date. Since Clio allows these dates to differ (e.g., time entries logged on different days than the bill date), QBD rejects the import with errors

1307.author: Qasim Khan
1307.text: Solution: When importing the IIF file into QuickBooks Desktop, the user should select the link that says "Import it for me. I'll fix it later" (usually located under the "Import without review" text). This forces the import despite the date mismatches

1307.author: Qasim Khan
1307.text: I know that If the "Import it for me" option fails, check the IIF file for special characters (such as @, :, or &) in the client's address or name fields. These can sometimes cause "Invalid IIF record type" errors.

1319.text: Or If there is a "No Charge" or "0.00" time entry on the bill, Clio might omit the unit count for that line to avoid a $0 calculation error.

1350.author: Service Cloud
1350.text: Additional context for this swarm (if provided) can be found below:Customer has a bill for 11239 with 13 percent tax and the customer was charged 82.81 accrued interest. Customer is saying the interest should only be for 4 days and the interest was calculated for 34 days. Why did clio charge 82.81 ? The  payment profile is 7 percent interest simple annually and 30 day grace period and issue date is 11/30/2025 and due date is 01/03/2026• Manual Override: By manually setting the Due Date to 01/03/2026, the "Grace Period" was effectively extended to 34 days. Manually entering a Due Date overrides the default Grace Period setting in the Payment Profile,.• The Calculation (Total Balance):    ◦ Principal + Tax: 11,239+1312,700.07**    ◦ Rate: 7% (0.07)    ◦ Time: 34 days (Nov 30 to Jan 3)    ◦ Formula: 12,700.07 x 0.07 x (34 / 365) = ~$82.81Solution: If the customer only wants to charge interest starting after the first 30 days:1. Void the current bill.2. Regenerate the bill.3. Ensure the Due Date field is left blank or check "Use contact's grace period". This forces the system to use the 30-day grace period from the profile.4. The system will then set the Due Date to Dec 30. Interest will begin accruing on Dec 31 (covering the first 30 days), or if they want to waive the first month, they must adjust their payment profile strategy (e.g., 0% interest for the first period), though standard functionality charges for the grace period once it expireThe issue is the customer wants a due date, and when checking the "use contact's grace period" it removes the due date. Cx wants due date and effectively charge interest after the grace period

1350.author: Marie Marasigan
1350.text: Hey RomeThe issue is the customer wants a due date, and when checking the “use contact’s grace period” it removes the due dateThis is expected as it will automatically calculate the due date and interest based off the Contact’s payment profile. The calculated due date will be presented on the bill.If you are unchecking that box and adding a custom due date then it will calculate interest to start after that ‘custom’ date that was entered

1371.author: Qasim Khan
1371.text: This issue occurs because Clio’s auto-numbering logic always looks for the highest existing internal "Number" in the system and increments it by one. Even if the "Display Number" shows a lower value, the system detects the internal values in the 20,000s introduced by the import and generates the next number accordingly.

1371.author: Hassan Jama
1371.text: So there is nothing we can do?

1371.author: Hassan Jama
1371.text: Just wanted to confirm

1371.author: Qasim Khan
1371.text: So essnetially, you cannot simply adjust the "Next matter number" setting to a lower value; that setting only supports increasing the sequence.

1371.author: Qasim Khan
1371.text: So to resume at 13349, you must remove or renumber the matters holding the high internal numbers so that 13348 becomes the highest number in the database.

1371.author: Qasim Khan
1371.text: Which means overriding some Matters first

1371.author: Qasim Khan
1371.text: This is the workarund

1415.author: Gosia Jamka
1415.text: Ok, checked Notebook, and this is what I got:The discrepancy in the contact count is likely because the Location filter in Clio Grow Email Marketing targets the Matter Location field, not the contact's physical address state.In Clio Grow, "Location" is a specific field found in Settings > Matters (often used for court locations or incident locations) and assigned to specific Matters.

1415.author: Gosia Jamka
1415.text: The Email Campaign filter for "Location" looks for contacts associated with Matters that have that specific Matter Location assigned. It does not look at the "State/Province" field in the contact's address block.The 34 contacts showing up likely have a Matter where the "Location" field was explicitly set to "CA". The other contacts have "CA" in their address, but their Matter "Location" field is likely blank or different.

1415.author: Gosia Jamka
1415.text: As a workaround it is suggested to either use contact tag or update matters- edit the matters for the missing contacts and assign the "CA" location to them!

1418.author: Gosia Jamka
1418.text: Ok, checked with the Notebook, and found this:If the Utilization Rate is showing an extremely high percentage (e.g., 10,000%), it is almost certainly because the Working Days setting in the user's Personal Performance profile was previously set to a very low number (e.g., 0 or 1).This creates a near-zero denominator for the calculation (Billable Hours / Available Working Hours), resulting in a massive percentage.Since you have already updated the Working Days to a standard number (e.g., 260), the persistence of the issue is likely due to data caching.Why hasn't it updated yet?• Caching Delay: The Firm and Personal Dashboards do not update instantly when settings are changed. The performance metrics and detailed annual report data update once an hour.• Solution: The customer needs to wait approximately one hour for the system to recalculate the metrics based on the new "Working Days" value.• Refresh: You can also ask them to click the refresh button on the dashboard page, though the backend calculation often relies on the hourly job.

1439.author: Graeme Clark
1439.text: Just posting this here for reference and so it might get picked up by Notebook.This has been resolved.As an FYI this was caused by a change that was made, but also likely caused by the user's system time being incorrect. I was able to reproduce by setting my computer's time forward or back (which caused the negative timer).When a timer is started, it is done on our backend. The backend server returns the start time of the timer. The timer was then calculating the elapsed time based on that compared to the system time.So if I set my system time 3 minutes fast, and start a timer a 1:03 (computer time), the backend would return that the timer started at 1:00 (which is the correct time). The front end then uses that time to show the elapsed time, but would basically be going "If this timer started at 1:00, and it's now 1:03, then 3 minutes has passed, so show that on the timer".When the timer is stopped though, the timer then returns an elapsed time fully based on the server time, and that is set as the QTY for the activity, so should be the correct amount. The timer is really just a visual aid. The actual timer is fully based on time on the server. (edited)

1463.author: Dani Heavenor
1463.text: The error “Enter a valid security code to continue” during MFA setup in Clio Manage could be one of these issues:1. Device/System Clock Out of Sync: TOTP-based MFA relies on the device’s clock being accurately synced to the official time. Even a small drift (e.g. 30 seconds) can cause codes to be rejected. This is the most common root cause, as confirmed in multiple internal discussions (,,,).Solution: Ensure the device used for generating codes (phone/computer) has automatic time sync enabled and matches the current time.2. Old/Incorrect Token Used: If the user is trying to use a previously saved token in their authenticator app (e.g. Google Authenticator, 1Password), it will generate invalid codes after re-enabling MFA.Solution: Remove any old Clio tokens from the authenticator app and scan the new QR code provided during setup.3. Timezone Mismatch: While the timezone itself doesn’t need to match Clio’s, it must be correct for the user’s location.4. App/Browser Issues: Rarely, browser extensions or security software can interfere with the setup flow.Solution: Try setup in an incognito/private window and disable extensions.

1534.author: Ebimo Rexford
1534.text: From Notebook:Likely Cause: The calendar events were migrated or imported using a different timezone setting than the one currently selected in the user's Clio profile. When the user accepted the prompt to update/match their timezone, Clio automatically adjusted the display time of those existing events based on the new offset (e.g., shifting from ET to PT would cause a 3-hour shift).Solution: There is no native "batch-edit" or "batch-shift" tool for calendar event times available to users in Clio Manage.Recommended Actions:1. Contact Data Migrations: If the migration was recent, the Data Migrations team may be able to re-import the calendar data with the correct timezone parameters to fix the anchor time. Start a thread in the migrations channel.2. Manual Adjustment: If a re-import is not possible, the user will need to manually edit the events to the correct time.Next Step: Start a consult with the Data Migrations team to verify if a re-import is feasible before advising manual work.

1561.text: Additional context for this swarm (if provided) can be found below:This issue typically happens when there are old, unaccepted invitations in the system for that email address. The system tries to link the new invite to an existing User ID (UUID), but if that ID is tied to a different or "released" email, the user will be prompted to log in with that wrong email.Steps to Resolve:1. Incognito Mode: First, ask the user to right-click the "Accept Invite" link and select Open in Incognito/Private Window. This ensures browser caching isn't causing the redirect.2. Internal Fix: If the issue persists, the old invitations must be cleared from the backend.    ◦ Start a #help-cs-consult.    ◦ Request that Technical Escalations (TE) expire all existing invitations for gabrielle.wolf@und.edu in Identity.3. Resend: Once TE confirms the invites are expired:    ◦ Have the firm administrator delete the pending invite in Clio Manage.    ◦ Resend a fresh invitation.    ◦ The user should accept the new invite immediately (preferably in Incognito).

1594.author: Matthew Tai
1594.text: From my research:If you connect Clio Grow to your email via SMTP, whether sent emails appear in the “Sent” folder in Outlook depends on the behaviour of the SMTP server/provider you are using.Clio Grow sends emails through the SMTP server, but not all SMTP providers automatically save outgoing messages to the “Sent” folder. Some providers do this by default, while others do not. This is a known limitation and has been discussed internally—users have reported that with certain providers (e.g., IONOS), sent emails do not appear in the “Sent” folder after SMTP integration, even though the emails are delivered successfully. This is not something Clio Grow can control directly, as the saving of sent messages is handled by the mail server, not by Grow itself.

1597.text: Hey @andrea.clareI had a similar call, and I found this in Notebook.Clio is legally required by the IRS to file Form 1099-K for any firm that meets specific processing thresholds through Clio Payments,. Because this is a federal regulatory requirement, firms cannot opt out of the filing,.Filing Thresholds & RequirementsThe requirement to file is determined by the total gross volume processed in a calendar year:• 2024: More than $5,000.• 2025: More than $2,500.• 2026: More than $600.• Transactions: A minimum of 200 transactions is also required,.Authorization & Process• Agreement: When firms originally sign up for Clio Payments, they must agree to receive the 1099-K as part of the application process.• Automatic Filing: In certain states, Clio automatically e-files the form to both the IRS and the state tax agency to satisfy combined reporting requirements,.• Data Source: The 1099-K reflects all gross amounts processed through Clio Payments, regardless of whether the firm categorized the funds as revenue or trust deposits.

1603.author: Zobair Ahmed
1603.text: Hi @shakeel.ahmed.syed just wanted to jump in,Matters imported directly into Clio Manage do not automatically sync back to Clio Grow. While Contacts sync bi-directionally (once opted in), Matters typically flow only from Grow to Manage.For historical data imported only to Manage, there is no "link" to a Grow matter because the matter record does not exist in Grow.You can export data from both systems (Manage and Grow) to CSV and compare them using Excel (VLOOKUP) to identify gaps. (edited)

1650.author: Gosia Jamka
1650.text: To resolve this, the customer must recover the deleted Contact and Matter. The system prevents voiding bills or removing associated items (like Credit Notes or Payments) if the parent Contact or Matter does not exist.1. Identify the Client: Open the Bill Preview (View Bill) and look for the Client Name listed on the invoice.2. Recover the Contact: Go to Settings > Recovery Bin. Filter by Contact, search for that name, and click Recover. (Do the same for the Matter if needed).3. Remove Credit Note/Payment: Once the Contact/Matter is active again, return to the Bill.    ◦ The Credit Note should now be visible/accessible in the Credit Notes tab. Delete it.    ◦ If there are any hidden payments preventing the void, they should become accessible or the error might resolve once the credit note is gone.4. Void the Bill: With the Credit Note removed, select More Actions > Void.5. Clean Up: Once the bill is voided, the customer can re-delete the Contact and Matter.

1660.author: Sohaib Naseem
1660.text: Overview of Issue We have completed a comprehensive technical review regarding the persistent calendar events on Michelle’s calendar that originated from Ron’s schedule. Despite revoking editor permissions and attempting a system-level "Calendar Reset," the events remain visible.Technical Root Cause The issue stems from how data ownership is established within the Clio database:Physical Record Creation: While Michelle held "Editor" permissions, the events were not merely being viewed; they were physically saved to her specific account database with the "Save to" field set to her name.Severed Connection: When Ron removed the editor permissions, it successfully stopped future syncing. However, it did not "un-write" the events already saved to Michelle's ledger.Independent Data: Because these events are now saved under Michelle's ownership, they are entirely independent of Ron’s calendar. Deleting the events on Ron’s side will have no effect on Michelle’s view.Why a Backend "Bulk Delete" is Not Possible We understand the time commitment required for manual deletion; however, a backend script cannot be safely executed for the following reasons:Data Integrity Risks: There is no automated way for the system to distinguish between a "Ron event" Michelle wants removed and a "Michelle event" she created herself during that same period.Liability of Data Loss: A backend wipe is permanent and irreversible. To prevent the accidental deletion of Michelle’s legitimate court dates or deadlines, the system requires a user to manually verify and select the items for removal.Reset Limitations: The "Bulk Reset" tool is designed to target standard synced data. Because these entries were saved to her primary calendar as manual adjustments, the tool bypasses them to prevent unintentional data loss.Recommended Resolution The most efficient way to clear these records is to use the Calendar List View in Clio Manage. This allows Michelle to filter for these specific events and delete them in batches of 50 at a time, significantly reducing the hours required for one-by-one deletion.

1667.author: Benison Joseph
1667.text: We know why it's failing. Which is also the reason why we don't guarantee success when recovering deleted items from recovery bin. Every element created in Clio could have multiple associations, some are created by Customer, some are built by us internally. Like you delete a matter and multiple items associated to it gets deleted. Now when you try to recover something that is tied to that deleted matter, it will fail because some associations tied to element is not available and is in deleted state or does not exist anymore.It's same in this case, it's not a recovery failure, the recovery was successful but the membership_entry which ties the recovered event to a calendar does not exist and hence it's not displayed.If the task works, we can check with devs to see if they have another workaround to reinstate those calendar memberships as a whole but no promises can be made

1684.text: We don’t need RA since this isn’t happening on their account or can’t be reproduced. All we need is the bill_id and details of the specific activity/screenshot to investigate this which was the ask on previous consult as well.Anyways I was able to find the bill_id and take a look. Custom rate is what the cx types in on the activity entry modal under “Rate” section. This is not something you can preset. Please go through this HC article for more details on rate hierarchy.From what I went through, I guess customers' concern is that the matter rate is not applied when creating activities and instead defaults to a random number. You mentioned “Confirmed Custom Rate is active at the Client level” but matter rate supersedes client rate and also i don’t see a rate set at client level so not sure what the Customer means by this.So the activity in question was created on Dec 17, 2025 @ 20:41:00.861 EST and we can see the rate on that activity when created was $1095. Can confirm through DI that the matter rate was set as $1195 for user 344859475 and another user under this matter 1741020023 and has remained unedited since 29th oct.Therefore, ideally if no edits were made on the time entry modal to rate section, the activity must be created with rate $1195.I looked at the GET request to /api/v4/activity_descriptions endpoint when this activity was created and can confirm that the rate for matter_id 1741020023 was fetched. Unfortunately we don’t know what went on customers’ screen but we can confirm from logs that we indeed fetched the matter rate and populated the time entry modal with that rate which was $1195 at that time.The only possibility I see is that there could be an activity description tied to the activity when it was created but does not exist now. The logs says "activity_description"=>"[FILTERED]" but this could also be the case when activity description is left nil so we cannot say that with certain.The only edit on the activity is from 29th Dec when the price was updated from 1095 to 1195; likely they removed the activity description as well then. Matter rates supersedes activity category rates and therefore the rate of activity category as well must default to $1195 but we don't have a way to confirm this from logs since activity category is redacted and also is removed/does not exist now. Hence the only possibilities are either the customer manually edited the rate to 1095 when they created the time entry (which is more likely or there could be a activity category acting rouge which is causing this which was tied to the activity when created.If the Customer can confirm that the only edit they made on 29th Dec was price and did not remove any activity category, then i guess we are left with only one possibility which is user error.

1739.text: This error indicates that the user's email address or domain has not been correctly added to the firm's Single Sign-On (SSO) configuration rules within Clio. Ensure the user's specific Email or Domain is listed in the Add section. 1752.text: @dani.heavenor @sohaib.naseem I found a work around! To bulk delete entries in both Outlook and Clio Manage, use the Classic Outlook App:Switch View: Navigate to Calendar > View > Change View > List.Select: Use Ctrl to select multiple items or drag to highlight a range. You can also de-select the entries you want to keep.Action: Right-click and select Delete.Because his calendar was synced to Clio, doing this deleted the tasks in bulk from both Clio Manage and and his outlook!It's not as fast as bulk deleting duplicates, but much faster then deleting one by one

1773.author: Zobair Ahmed
1773.text: Hello @ranita.singh Clio Launcher is not a collaborative tool. Unlike Google Docs or Microsoft 365 Online, there is no "live" cursor. cx usually works on a downloaded temporary copy on their device.The document displayed in the main Documents tab in Clio will always reflect the last person to click save.Clio never deletes the existing work. If Person 2 saves over Person 1, Person 1's file becomes a "previous version" stored in the Version History, but their changes are removed from the current active document.

1773.author: Service Cloud
1773.text: A swarm member record was created in Salesforce for each swarm member:  @zobair.ahmed.

1773.author: Ranita Singh
1773.text: @zobair.ahmed So based on your information above, Person 2 is currently editing version 1 of the document - they won't be able to see changes made by Person 1 who has saved a new change to version 1 > as result changed to version 2.The only solution is that Person 1 will need to advise Person 2 that they have updated the document and then Person 2 will need to reopen the updated document again and edit that second/new version. Please confirm this specific scenario Scenario and query from Customer: If Person 1 is working on a document and saves the document (now this will be version 2) while version 1 is still open with Person 2 - will Person 2 get the updated version (that has been saved by Person 1)?Further to this, the question here is if Version 1 has been updated to Version 2 by Person 1 ~ have the changes been received by Person 2 while he was editing version 1. Please confirm the result here.

1773.author: Zobair Ahmed
1773.text: @ranita.singh You are absolutely correct. Person 2 will not receive updates while they are editing Version 1. Clio Launcher downloads a temporary copy to the local device; it does not maintain a live connection to the file in the cloud while it is open.Person 2 must close their document without saving, if they want to avoid overwriting and open the file again to download Version 2.In more details:Person 2 is working on that isolated, downloaded copy. Their computer is not "listening" for changes made by Person 1 in the cloud. When Person 1 clicks save, Clio Launcher uploads that file as Version 2. Person 2 is still looking at their local download of version 1.If Person 2 subsequently saves their document, Clio will upload it as Version 3. This Version 3 will contain only person 2's changes, effectively "hiding" Person 1's work in the Version History.

1792.author: Dan Kotak
1792.text: SureSteps to Resolve1. Verify Email Match: Ensure the email address logged into the Outlook account matches the Clio Manage login email exactly. A mismatch will cause the authentication flow to fail and reset.2.Clear Browser Cache and Cookies: Perform a hard refresh or clear the browser cache. If the loop occurs on the Outlook Desktop app, clear the Edge WebView2 or RoamCache folder on the computer.3.Test via Web Browser: Have the user attempt to connect the sync via a web browser (e.g., Chrome or Edge) instead of the Outlook Desktop app to isolate if the issue is application-specific.4.Check for GoDaddy/Exchange: If the firm’s email is hosted through GoDaddy, this is a known limitation. The authentication token often fails to return to Clio on the desktop app. Workaround: Use Outlook on the web.5.Disable Pop-up Blockers: Ensure the browser is not automatically closing the authentication window before it can pass the token back to Clio.6. Full Re-authentication: Log out of Clio Manage and Office 365 entirely, then restart the connection process from the Clio Manage Settings page.If the loop persists after testing multiple browsers and clearing cache, please start a#help-cs-consult and provide the Manage User ID.

1804.author: Keturah B.W.
1804.text: Now that I have everything written out this is the insight I received when I asked for assistance from Consult Notebook. Clio’s auto-numbering logic always looks for the highest existing internal "Number" (Column B in a CSV export) in the system and increments it by one. Because you have a matter with the internal number 139 (line 69), the system will naturally suggest 140 for the next matter, regardless of what the "Display Number" shows. The "Next matter number will start from" setting only allows you to increase the sequence; it cannot force the system to start at a lower number if a higher one already exists in the databaseWorkaround to Align the Sequence:1. Identify High Numbers: Export a full Matter list as a CSV (including closed/archived matters)Sort by the Number column to find every matter with a value higher than 682. Manually Override: The customer must use the Matter Number Override tool (Settings > Firm Preferences > Matter Numbering) for every matter that has an internal number higher than 683. Renumber to Lower Values: Change those high numbers (like 139) to a lower, unused sequence.4. Set Starting Point: Once no matters exist with an internal number higher than 68, the customer can set the "Next matter number will start from" to 69Important Note: There is currently no backend tool to perform these renumbering overrides in bulk; the customer must update them individually. Additionally, ensure the customer does not have any deleted matters in the Recovery Bin with high numbers, as these also block the sequence. If the customer finds this process too time-consuming, they may need to use Manual matter numbering moving forward to have total control over the string. (edited)

1809.text: @munir.ibrahim I think this is just a pretty simple case of the user entering in these payments themselves. All the payments have a "Payment Date" that is backdated.Payments on the payment tab, and on the transactions tab are sorted by the payment date, not the date they were actually entered into Clio (aka the creation date), so if there are payments with the same date and amount entered, it can kind of look like a duplicate.Between 11:28 and 11:44, 28 payments were added to the bill with different payment dates.
