1895.text: Additional context for this swarm (if provided) can be found below:- What's the end goal?Customer is looking to understand how to resolve balances and payments in QuickBooks, as items under Undeposited Funds are still appearing there even though the data has already been matched in bank account and reconciled.- When/where is it happening? (List steps) Cx needs assistance with QBO. While reviewing the November & December Reconciliation Report and Undeposited Funds in QBO, the customer noticed that there over 75 pages of Clio payment deposit still appearing in Undeposited Funds even though it has already been tracked and reconciled in QBO. The customer wants to understand why funds that are already matched are still showing up in Undeposited Funds section of Quickbooks and how to fix it.• Cx was able to login to colleague admin account to view bill sync stast QuickBooks Online error code (6540), (6480) - Cx wants believe Quickbooks is causing duplicates - What have you tried?     - Troubleshooting steps taken Provided Cx insight from consult notebook: Why Funds Remain in Undeposited FundsBy design, all bill payments recorded in Clio sync to the Undeposited Funds account in QuickBooks Online (QBO). This account acts as a temporary holding area until the firm is ready to record the actual deposit into their bank account.If funds appear reconciled but still show up in Undeposited Funds, it is typically due to one of the following:• Missing "Bank Deposit" Step: Matching a transaction in the bank feed does not automatically clear the individual payments out of Undeposited Funds. In QBO, the user must manually create a Bank Deposit to group those payments and move them from Undeposited Funds into the Operating Account.• Duplicate Records: If the bank feed downloaded a transaction and the user categorized it manually instead of matching it to the Clio-synced record, the original synced payment will remain in Undeposited Funds as an open, "created" item.• Payment Edits: Deleting or editing a payment in Clio treats it as a new transaction. If the original payment was already deposited or locked in QBO, the sync may fail to remove the old record, leaving a "phantom" entry in Undeposited FundRecommended Workaround1. Check for Duplicates: Look for two entries of the same amount—one that is "Reconciled" and one that is still in "Created" status in the Undeposited Funds ledger.2. Align Data: If the firm has already reconciled the bank statement using a manual entry, they may need to delete the duplicate synced entry in QBO to zero out the ledger.3. Future Workflow: Advise the firm to avoid manually creating deposits or marking bills as paid in QBO. They should record the payment in Clio first, let it sync to Undeposited Funds, and then use the "Bank Deposit" feature in QBO to link it to their bank statement     - Reproduced in demo?     - Link to resources used     - Relevant screenshots/media (e.g. dev tools) https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/18DgEMx9jhixBqEHBIAM1McEaM9jgVI6E?usp=drive_link- What do you need/where are you stuck? Customer asked for a call back from an intermediate rep to review with her after spendig an hour together over the phone. Advised the customer of the three main reasons funds may remain in Undeposited Funds. The customer initially only had billing account access and did not have admin access, so we were unable to check the sync status to confirm whether there were any errors related to the payment she was reviewing in Undeposited Funds. Later in the call, the customer asked a colleague to provide their user profile so we could review the billing sync settings.

1895.text: I just asked consult notebook: After payments have been match to Cx bank account in QBO and Reconciled is it common for payment to still show up in QBO Undeposited Funds.They answer I got:It is common for payments to remain in Undeposited Funds if the user has not completed the manual "Bank Deposit" step in QuickBooks Online (QBO)By design, all bill payments recorded in Clio sync to the Undeposited Funds account, which acts as a temporary holding area until the firm records the actual deposit into their bank account                                                                                                                                      Manual Categorization: If a user "adds" or "categorizes" a bank feed transaction manually instead of "matching" it to the Clio-synced record, the original synced payment remains in Undeposited Funds as an open itemDuplicate Records: If the firm has already reconciled their bank statement using a manual entry, the Clio-synced record will appear as a "phantom" duplicate entry in the ledge

1975.text: Additional context for this swarm (if provided) can be found below:As per NB: • Sync/Feature Flag Mismatch: The account's feature flag state for custom roles may not have synchronized correctly with the Permissions Service.    ◦ Action: Start a #help-cs-consult to have Technical Escalations (TE) run a backfill job, specifically AdminJob::BackfillPermissionsServiceWithAccountsFeatureFlagState for the affected account ID.• Identity UUID Issues: If the user's email was recently changed or unlinked, the Permissions Service might still be associated with an old UUID, causing a lookup failure.    ◦ Action: Start a #help-cs-consult for TE to update the user’s data and map it to the correct login record.• Clio Connect Conflicts: If the PS also has an active Clio Connect user associated with the same email, the system may incorrectly apply restricted portal permissions.    ◦ Action: Verify if the user has an active Clio Connect identity and consider disabling it to unblock access.• Stale Cache: Permission updates may take up to 10 minutes to reflect, or the browser may be holding stale data.    ◦ Action: Perform a full browser cache clear and test in an incognito window. Specialists can also try clicking the Refresh Permission Cache button on the user's page in the Admin Panel.• Plan Eligibility: Only Advanced and Complete plans support unlimited custom roles; Essentials is limited to two. Ensure the customer is on an eligible tier.I had a dev thread for redirects on Roles and permissions for this case as well: https://clio.slack.com/archives/C032GADELJZ/p1767215842298839 but they have reported the fix is deployed so I am unsure if that'd be relevant here^

1981.author: Matthew Tai
1981.text: I’m assuming that yes is in response to the error message From notebook (accurate):Saving files directly to Clio Drive using “Print to PDF” functions (such as Microsoft Print to PDF or Adobe PDF) is a known limitation for Windows users due to how those applications interact with the WebDAV protocolTroubleshooting & Workarounds (as of: Oct 2025)• Save Locally First (Recommended): Instead of printing directly to the Drive folder, save the PDF to your desktop or downloads folder first. Once saved, drag and drop the file into the desired Clio Drive matter foldere .• Use “Save As” PDF: Within Microsoft Word, try using File > Save As and selecting PDF as the file format instead of using the “Print” menu. This often bypasses the restrictions found in the print dialogued.• Clio Manage Alternative: Upload the original Word document to Clio Manage through the web UI and use the Create PDF option from the document’s dropdown menuo .• File via Outlook Add-in: If you are converting an attachment from an email, use the Clio Outlook Add-in to file the document directly to the matter, which handles the transfer via a more stable protocolWhy this is happening: This behavior is tied to a known bug (INC-000000891 / DMSEXP-847) where third-party PDF managers and specific Microsoft updates create 0KB or corrupted files when saving directly to a network-mounted driveHere’s the bug incident mentioned:https://themis-solutions.lightning.force.com/lightning/r/Incident/0nyOG0000001fnVYAQ/view

1994.author: Kajal Harijan
1994.text: @stephen.yorke Here is what I found:The error "BucketAlreadyExists" during S3 bucket creation means the requested bucket name is already taken—S3 bucket names are globally unique across all AWS accounts and regions. This is a well-documented AWS constraint: once a bucket name is used, no other account can use it until it's deleted, regardless of region.The additional error about the bucket not being found in the US East region, and the "AuthorizationHeaderMalformed" message, typically occurs when the bucket name is already registered in a different region. AWS expects the CreateBucket call to target the region where the bucket name is already in use, but since it's not available, the operation fails.Key points and solutions:- S3 bucket names must be globally unique. If the name is taken, you cannot use it—even if you can't see or access the bucket.- The error message and AWS documentation both recommend changing the bucket name. This is the only solution—there is no way to force creation with a non-unique name.- Clio's best practice is to append the Clio region to the bucket name to ensure uniqueness

1994.author: Stephen Yorke
1994.text: Hey @kajalben.harijan - thanks for looking in to this. I had found the same info and had asked the Cx to look for a bucket with the same name across all of their regions. They've confirmed that "no bucket exists with the name "Data-escrow-clio-us-justicecentrehong" in any of the regions in America, Asia Pacific, Canada, Europe nor South America"Additionally, when it comes to changing the name, I had asked Notebook about this and it said it is not possible for customers to do this:As of: December 2025, it is not possible for customers to change, rename, or choose their own Amazon S3 bucket name for Data Escrow in Clio Manage.Key Details• Automatic Naming: Clio automatically generates a unique bucket name for every account (e.g., data-escrow-clio-us-[AccountID]-[RandomString])• Security Restriction: The ability for users to specify their own bucket names was removed to prevent security risks, such as data overlapping between accounts• Workflow: Customers should not create a bucket manually in their AWS console. They simply provide the Access Key and Secret Key, and Clio will create and name the bucket automatically during the connection processBased on this, how would we move this forward?

2093.author: Ro Paydar
2093.text:
But as mentioned -- trying to attach a document from Clio Drive is not advised as the intended use case for Clio Drive.Clio Drive and the Clio Desktop App as a whole are presented as document file-sharing and file-management products.In the help center article for Clio Desktop App, there is a brief description of what Clio Drive is / what it does:Clio Drive is a virtual drive where you can create, access, and edit documents in files and folders right from your desktop.
Clio Drive syncs between your computer and Clio Manage, which makes it easier to collaborate across your firm. You can make changes in either Clio Drive or Clio Manage, and those changes will be mirrored.The main point to highlight is that it is a "virtual drive". The functionality of this drive is to create documents, access documents, and edit documents. The sync point is between the virtual drive in a computer and Clio Manage.How can customers access their documents? In the file explorer (localhost), they can click on the file name for the document they wish to access. At this point, the document is not actually on their computer. What they see on the virtual drive is a list of document names that correspond to the document that is located in Clio Manage.The document is downloaded from Clio, to their computer. The document is then automatically opened by the default program for viewing documents (typically Microsoft Word). Important to note:Accessing files is not the same as having the files stored. Most people confuse Clio Drive with tools like OneDrive or Google Drive. This is not the same as Clio Drive.Example: if the customer accessed the file from Clio Drive, saved it directly to their local computer, and then tried to access the file or attach it to an email, it would work.This is because the file is stored to the actual computer. The file is directly accessible when adding it as an email attachment.The main purpose of Clio Drive is to allow firms to make quick edits to documents and to work asynchronously among firm members. Unfortunately, many customers mistakenly treat this as a file storage solution, which it is not.Let me know if this makes sense  @tunde.lawal (edited)

Check for Previous Syncs: Confirm with the customer if the firm or a firm owner previously used a different Clio account. 2182.text: Additional context for this swarm (if provided) can be found below:- What's the end goal?Customer is looking to understand how to resolve balances and payments in QuickBooks, as items under Undeposited Funds are still appearing there even though the data has already been matched in bank account and reconciled.- When/where is it happening? (List steps) Cx needs assistance with QBO. While reviewing the November & December Reconciliation Report and Undeposited Funds in QBO, the customer noticed that there over 75 pages of Clio payment deposit still appearing in Undeposited Funds even though it has already been tracked and reconciled in QBO. The customer wants to understand why funds that are already matched are still showing up in Undeposited Funds section of Quickbooks and how to fix it.• Cx was able to login to colleague admin account to view bill sync stast QuickBooks Online error code (6540), (6480) - Cx wants believe Quickbooks is causing duplicates - What have you tried?     - Troubleshooting steps taken Provided Cx insight from consult notebook: Why Funds Remain in Undeposited FundsBy design, all bill payments recorded in Clio sync to the Undeposited Funds account in QuickBooks Online (QBO). This account acts as a temporary holding area until the firm is ready to record the actual deposit into their bank account.If funds appear reconciled but still show up in Undeposited Funds, it is typically due to one of the following:• Missing "Bank Deposit" Step: Matching a transaction in the bank feed does not automatically clear the individual payments out of Undeposited Funds. In QBO, the user must manually create a Bank Deposit to group those payments and move them from Undeposited Funds into the Operating Account.• Duplicate Records: If the bank feed downloaded a transaction and the user categorized it manually instead of matching it to the Clio-synced record, the original synced payment will remain in Undeposited Funds as an open, "created" item.• Payment Edits: Deleting or editing a payment in Clio treats it as a new transaction. If the original payment was already deposited or locked in QBO, the sync may fail to remove the old record, leaving a "phantom" entry in Undeposited FundRecommended Workaround1. Check for Duplicates: Look for two entries of the same amount—one that is "Reconciled" and one that is still in "Created" status in the Undeposited Funds ledger.2. Align Data: If the firm has already reconciled the bank statement using a manual entry, they may need to delete the duplicate synced entry in QBO to zero out the ledger.3. Future Workflow: Advise the firm to avoid manually creating deposits or marking bills as paid in QBO. They should record the payment in Clio first, let it sync to Undeposited Funds, and then use the "Bank Deposit" feature in QBO to link it to their bank statement     - Reproduced in demo?     - Link to resources used     - Relevant screenshots/media (e.g. dev tools) https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/18DgEMx9jhixBqEHBIAM1McEaM9jgVI6E?usp=drive_link- What do you need/where are you stuck? Customer asked for a call back from an intermediate rep to review with her after spendig an hour together over the phone. Advised the customer of the three main reasons funds may remain in Undeposited Funds. The customer initially only had billing account access and did not have admin access, so we were unable to check the sync status to confirm whether there were any errors related to the payment she was reviewing in Undeposited Funds. Later in the call, the customer asked a colleague to provide their user profile so we could review the billing sync settings.I just asked consult notebook: After payments have been match to Cx bank account in QBO and Reconciled is it common for payment to still show up in QBO Undeposited Funds.They answer I got:

2182.author: Service Cloud
2182.text: It is common for payments to remain in Undeposited Funds if the user has not completed the manual "Bank Deposit" step in QuickBooks Online (QBO)By design, all bill payments recorded in Clio sync to the Undeposited Funds account, which acts as a temporary holding area until the firm records the actual deposit into their bank account                                                                                                                                      Manual Categorization: If a user "adds" or "categorizes" a bank feed transaction manually instead of "matching" it to the Clio-synced record, the original synced payment remains in Undeposited Funds as an open itemDuplicate Records: If the firm has already reconciled their bank statement using a manual entry, the Clio-synced record will appear as a "phantom" duplicate entry in the ledgePrevious swarm was missed: https://clio.slack.com/archives/C62SC017F/p1768435020123759?thread_ts=1768435019.970999&cid=C62SC017F

2182.author: Kajal Harijan
2182.text: 1. Clio's Role: Clio syncs bill payments to the Undeposited Funds account in QuickBooks Online (QBO)2. The Duplication: When the actual funds hit the bank account, the transaction appears in the QBO Bank Feed.    ◦ Correct Workflow: The user should click "Match" in the bank feed to link the bank deposit to the existing payment sitting in Undeposited Funds.    ◦ Customer's Workflow: The user likely clicked "Add" (or categorized) the transaction in the bank feed. This created a new, separate deposit record in QBO3. Result: The "Added" transaction was reconciled, but the original payment from Clio remains stuck in "Undeposited Funds," causing the 75-page backlog.

2202.text: Additional context for this swarm (if provided) can be found below:Filings that are "immediately rejected" with an "Unknown" reason and lack the Refile button typically indicate a Failed submission (system or formatting error) rather than a standard Court Rejection (clerk denial).Why this happens• Failed vs. Rejected: The "Refile" feature (which preserves the original timestamp) is generally available only for filings Rejected by a clerk. "Failed" filings often do not reach the court's system to establish a valid timestamp to relate back to.• Common Causes: Immediate failures are frequently caused by special characters (e.g., &, #, %) in the document file name or file names that exceed character limits (typically over 100 characters).Next StepsBecause the customer needs to preserve the filing date and the standard "Refile" option is unavailable, you must investigate the specific failure reason on the backend.Please start a #help-cs-consult with the following details:1. Submission ID (found in the URL or E-filing tab).2. Date/Time of the attempt.3. Customer's specific request regarding the envelope number/filing date.

2272.text: So far checking around it can be caused for the following reasons:1. Incorrect Card Number Format: The number entered does not match the expected length or pattern for the card type. For example, American Express cards must have 15 digits and start with 34 or 37.2. Non-Numeric Characters: The input contains characters other than digits, spaces, or hyphens.3. Luhn Algorithm Failure: The card number fails the Luhn checksum, a standard algorithm used to validate credit card numbers. If the number doesn’t pass this check, it’s considered invalid regardless of format.4. Unsupported Card Type: The card type is not supported by the payment processor or the form’s validation library.In Clio’s implementation, a third-party library is used for this validation. The validation checks for:- Correct prefix (e.g., 34 or 37 for Amex)- Correct length (e.g., 15 digits for Amex)- Only allowed characters (digits, spaces, hyphens)- Passing the Luhn algorithmIt seems to be a Mastercard as you mentioned and its 16 digits (seems right). 2347.text: Additional context for this swarm (if provided) can be found below:-interest keeps getting added to the older bills in Clio - it looks like there was a default payment profile set up to add interest to bills but then the default PP was possibly edited to no longer charge interest - alot of contact has the default PP set up on their account and alot of their bills still take on the previous PP and is still charging the clients the interest even after the interest has been deleted from the bill and the PP has been updated to charge no interest- I am having the cx delete, regenerate and back date the bills to prevent the interest from being added to the bills,  but she said she has alot of bills and would rather not do that - do we have any other solutions?- according to Notebook a task can be ran for this issue

2347.text: are these old bills that have been Paid? Or are still Unpaid?

2347.author: Malisha Lewis
2347.text: It looks like most have been unpaid

2347.author: Dani Heavenor
2347.text: We have this task, but there are caveats:The following restrictions applyThe new interest rate has to be a value between 0.00 and 100.00 (no negative interest)If you have different interest rates for different bills, run the task for one interest rate at a time.All bills in the group below must belong to the same account otherwise they will be excluded from being processed.What the task will do:Sets a new interest on the bill (valid states: draft, awaiting approval, awaiting payment).Sets a new interest period on the bill.Sets a new interest type on the bill.Removes all interest line items on the bill.What the task will not do:Set new interest on bills with partial payments, or that are fully paid.Remove interest from bills that have partial payments, or that are fully paid.Deal with Trust Requests as Trust Requests don't accrue interest.Backfill the interest. The Generate Interest for Bills task needs to be run

2360.author: Service Cloud
2360.text: Additional context for this swarm (if provided) can be found below:-I found this : it is expected behavior for non-billable entries to be excluded from an invoice export in certain scenarios, particularly if you are using the LEDES format or Quick Bill.Common Reasons Non-Billables Do Not Appear on Exports• LEDES 1998B Export: If the "CSV" download is actually a LEDES 1998B file (often used for electronic billing), non-billable entries are automatically excluded. This is a known limitation of the LEDES format, as it does not include sections for non-billable items, even if they appear on the visual PDF bill in Clio.• Quick Bill Generation: If the invoice was created using the Quick Bill button, non-billable entries (even those marked "Show on Bill") are not included on the invoice at all. They only appear if the bill is generated using the New Bills (Bulk Billing) workflow.• Aggregated Bills: If the bill uses Activity Summary (aggregation) to combine line items, non-billable entries are intended to be excluded to avoid confusion with the calculated totals.WorkaroundIf the customer needs to show non-billable work on a CSV/LEDES export, they may need to:1. Edit the Entry: Change the entry to "Billable" but set the Rate to $0.00.2. Verify Format: Ensure the export format allows for $0 line items (some strict LEDES parsers may still reject this, but it is the primary workaround).

2442.author: Dan Kotak
2442.text: Based on the volume (850,000+), this was likely caused by a data import where a unique field (like a Description or Subject) was mapped to the "Category" column, causing the system to create a new category for every unique line item.Steps to Resolve1. Check for Recent Imports• Go to Settings > Imports.• Look for a recent import (likely Documents or Activities) that matches the timeline of when these categories appeared.• If found, click Undo on that import. This is the only way to bulk remove the data and the associated categories created by that specific job.2. Start a Consult• If the import is not visible or cannot be undone, start a #help-cs-consult immediately.• Do not attempt to delete these manually or via API script without guidance. Deleting this volume of data can cause significant database replication lag and system strain.• There is no "Bulk Delete" tool for Document Categories in the front-end UI

Do not select the "Boardroom" calendar [cite: 293, 296].Customer is worried that the calendar data will be deleted. 2474.author: Sonia Czerniawski
2474.text: In the context of Clio Payments, the status requires_confirmation (often seen in the Admin Panel or API responses) indicates that a payment flow has been initiated by the client but not yet fully completed or finalized with the payment provider.This status is most commonly associated with Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL/Affirm) and Tap to Pay transactions.What It Means• Stripe Mapping: This internal Clio status maps to the incomplete status in Stripe.• User Action: The client likely clicked the "Pay Later" button or started a Tap to Pay transaction, causing the system to create a payment record, but they closed the window, exited the flow, or failed to submit the final confirmation before the process was finished.What Happens Next?• If the client completes the steps: The status will update to Authorized and subsequently Completed once the funds are captured.• If the client does nothing: The transaction will remain in this state temporarily (usually around 1 hour) before automatically moving to Canceled.

2489.text: Customer email: ello, I have been working with my domain administrator (State of Ohio Department of Administrative Services) to get the Outlook connection to Clio set up properly. We got the connection with the Manage side to work, emails can be filed now and can be sent from Clio using our addresses. However we cannot get the connection to Grow established, with it continuing to throw the "Need admin approval" despite our admins setting up the permissions to what we think should be correct. Below is what they said:"OTC Technical Staff,OK, Jeremy and I both tried to use a PowerShell script to crowbar the permission in for admin consent on the Clio Grow Enterprise App and were unsuccessful (it returned an error 403, permission denied). Update-MgOauth2PermissionGrant : Insufficient privileges to complete the operation.Status: 403 (Forbidden)ErrorCode: Authorization_RequestDeniedI think we need you to file a support case with your vendor to identify why when an admin tries to "admin consent" the app, the permission scope is missing the Mail.ReadWrite permission.In the State's tenant, we do not allow users to consent to app consent requests for security and data protection reasons...so the consent type must be admin consented."Please advise why the admin consent is missing scope for MaiLReadWrite permission, and how we should proceed. If you would like me to send the PowerShell script they mentioned as well let me know. Best,

2489.author: Gray Siemens
2489.text: Notebook:It sounds like there is a specific permissions mismatch regarding the scope required for the Clio Grow integration versus what is being granted or requested during the admin consent process.Since your organization (State of Ohio) requires strict Admin Consent and restricts individual user consent, the Global Administrator needs to grant specific permissions for the Clio Grow application within their Microsoft Entra (Azure) Admin Center. The error Insufficient privileges to complete the operation usually indicates the account running the PowerShell script lacks the necessary roles to modify OAuth2 permission grants, or the scope they are trying to "crowbar" doesn't align with what the app is requesting.Here is how to proceed:For the Domain Administrator (IT):1. Verify Application ID: Ensure you are granting consent to the correct Enterprise Application. Clio Manage and Clio Grow use different tokens and application IDs.2. Grant Consent via Entra Admin Center (Preferred over PowerShell):    ◦ Log in to the Microsoft Entra Admin Center (formerly Azure Portal).    ◦ Navigate to Enterprise Applications.    ◦ Locate the application named Clio Grow (sometimes listed as "Clio Grow V4").    ◦ Click Permissions > Grant admin consent for [Organization Name].3. Required Scopes:    ◦ For email syncing/sending in Grow, the application requires the Mail.Send permission scope to send emails on behalf of the user.    ◦ If you are attempting to add Mail.ReadWrite, please note that Clio Grow's email integration primarily focuses on sending emails (SMTP/API based). The Outlook Add-in (used for filing/reading) is what typically requires Mail.ReadWrite and uses the Clio Manage token.    ◦ Ensure the admin consent coversoffline_access and User.Read as well.Next Steps: If the Admin has confirmed they granted consent via the GUI in Entra and users are still blocked, or if the PowerShell error persists, please start a #help-cs-consult. We may need to escalate this to our Technical Escalations team to review the specific scopes requested by the Grow application for your tenant. (edited)
